note: RIDDLER SEAT 9 — the stage. Riddle: everyone says more than they know and less than they mean, and the fool tells the truth. Soliloquy, wit-duels, fools. Equivalents ride this shelf (Marlowe, Melville, Joyce).
interactions: sources: Holinshed's Chronicles and North's Plutarch — the interactions are mostly with the dead
Marlowe: same playhouses, rival, Greene's 'upstart crow' (1592); Henry VI co-authorship is the live scholarly question
Voltaire imported him to France and spent decades apologizing for it (edge: voltaire shelf)
Tolstoy attacked ('Shakespeare and the Drama'); Orwell answered ('Lear, Tolstoy and the Fool', 1947) — one shelf defending another across a century (edge: orwell shelf)
Melville: Ahab's speeches are Shakespearean soliloquy in novel form; the storm chapters are Lear at sea
Joyce: Scylla & Charybdis (Ulysses 9) is a whole episode of Shakespeare theory; Ulysses = the stage turned inside out
Borges: 'Everything and Nothing' and Shakespeare's Memory (1983) — the man who was everybody and no one (edge: stephenson shelf)
